beats.subline: Tuesday, August 4, 2026 close — a broad rally pushed the S&P 500 to its first record in two months and the Dow above 54,000 for the first time.
beats.body: Strong earnings and hopes for progress on reopening the Strait of Hormuz fueled a broad tech comeback; Palantir soared roughly 29% on blowout revenue tied to AI demand, while SpaceX and AMD also reported earnings.

beats.headline: Iran and Oman near a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
beats.body: Regional officials said Iran and Oman have made progress on an interim agreement that would route Gulf-bound ships through an Iranian-controlled channel and outbound ships through an Omani-controlled one, with a formal announcement possibly coming this week; any deal is expected to be linked to the US lifting its naval blockade of Iranian ports.

beats.headline: China sanctions six US entities and tightens drone export controls ahead of expected Xi-Trump summit
beats.body: Beijing's Commerce Ministry announced countermeasures Wednesday against six American organizations, including Applied DNA Sciences and Human Rights in China, and imposed case-by-case scrutiny on drone-related exports to the US, in response to Washington's addition of 43 Chinese firms to a forced-labor import blacklist; the tit-for-tat comes weeks ahead of a planned Xi Jinping visit to the US.

beats.headline: US commanders warn missile-defense stockpiles are 'dangerously low' after Iran war
beats.body: Senior military officials told CNN the US has burned through nearly 80% of interceptors for a key missile-defense system and roughly half its Patriot interceptor inventory during the nearly six-month conflict with Iran, on top of a separate Reuters finding that Army long-range surface-to-surface missile stocks are nearly exhausted; officials say the depletion is raising concern about readiness for future crises involving Russia or China.

beats.headline: Navy reclassifies 19 Virginia-class submarines as guided-missile boats to reflect bigger strike punch
beats.body: The Navy is redesignating 19 planned Virginia-class submarines equipped with the Virginia Payload Module from fast-attack subs (SSN) to guided-missile submarines (SSGN), citing their expanded Tomahawk-class strike capacity of up to 65 weapons; the change applies to Block V and VI boats delivering through 2038, starting with the future USS Arizona.

beats.headline: Anthropic names former California Supreme Court justice as its first chief global affairs officer
beats.body: Anthropic appointed Mariano-Florentino 'Tino' Cuéllar, who previously led the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, to head policy and government relations worldwide, reporting to President Daniela Amodei; the hire comes as Anthropic works to repair friction with the Trump administration after the Pentagon labeled it a national-security 'supply chain risk' and briefly restricted export of its top models.

beats.headline: Cam Lewis shifts to safety as Coby Bryant's injury thins Bears' back end
beats.body: With Coby Bryant expected to miss 8-10 weeks and nickel corner Kyler Gordon still sidelined on the PUP list with a lingering calf injury, six-year veteran Cam Lewis has moved from nickel to safety alongside rookie Dillon Thieneman in 11-on-11 work, per ESPN's training-camp notebook; Lewis started at safety for Buffalo in last season's playoffs.

beats.headline: Byron heads into Iowa Speedway as the field's most consistent performer there
beats.body: Ahead of Sunday's Iowa Corn 350, Hendrick Motorsports notes William Byron carries the tour's best average finish at Iowa Speedway among active drivers, having finished runner-up in the track's inaugural Cup race and won there the following year; NASCAR remains on its scheduled break until the green flag drops this weekend.

beats.headline: No fresh news on this beat right now
beats.body: No new PCA-specific development from a reputable outlet surfaced within the 72-hour window beyond the June General Assembly news already reported in prior briefs.
